basis: jinshu:053:s0169 explicitly names 閻纘 as the person whose words moved the emperor to establish 思子台 in the aftermath of Minhuai’s death and funeral. zizhitongjian:083:s0200 explicitly names 西戎校尉司馬閻纘 bringing his coffin to the palace gate and pleading for 遹, comparing him with the Han wronged heir; s0201–s0202 continue that plea.

The rare identical full Chinese name 閻纘, same Emperor Hui/crown-prince Yu setting and specific advocacy for the wronged heir connect the two records. Tongjian s0197–s0198 explicitly gives 永康元年/300; s0204’s 纘，圃之孫也 continues the same named man. Jinshu’s funeral/terrace sequence is likewise current AD300 metadata. Yan Xun versus Yan Zuan is an English reading difference and does not establish two Chinese-named men.
